title: More time for an assessment (AUT)
about: Helps you work out whether to ask for a 3-day short extension or apply for special consideration at AUT, when to apply, what evidence you need and by when, and where to get help.

sources.name: Auckland University of Technology (AUT), Special consideration for an assessment

warning: This is AUT's guidance, for AUT students. If you study somewhere else, follow your own university's rules.
audience: AUT students who need more time for an assignment, or whose test or exam has been affected by something serious
version: AUT "Special consideration for an assessment" web page, no date or review date shown, read 19 Nov 2026

lines.text: If something serious and outside your control affects an assessment, you can apply for special consideration. You could also ask for a short extension of up to 3 days.

quotes.text: your ability to attempt or prepare for an assessment may be seriously affected by exceptional circumstances beyond your control.
If this happens, you can apply for special consideration for that assessment.
You could also apply for a short extension of up to 3 days

options.label: Just a couple of extra days
My due date (or test or exam) has already passed

steps.title: Can you get a short extension?

lines.text: A short extension gives you 3 calendar days. You don't need any evidence.

quotes.text: The short extension is for 3 calendar days
You don't need to provide evidence for a short extension.

lines.text: You can get one only if all three of these are true:
1. It's an assignment, not a test or exam. Nothing done under controlled conditions can have a short extension.

quotes.text: You can't apply for short extensions for tests and exams; any assessment conducted under controlled conditions is not eligible for a short extension

lines.text: 2. You haven't had a short extension in this course yet. You get one per course.

quotes.text: You can only have one short extension per course.

lines.text: 3. You apply by midnight the day BEFORE it's due. For example, if it's due at 4pm on Monday, apply before midnight on Sunday.

quotes.text: You must apply by midnight the day BEFORE your assessment is due
For example, if an assessment is due at 4pm on Monday 20 May, in order to be eligible for a short extension, you must apply BEFORE midnight on Sunday 19 May.

ask.question: Are all three true for you?

lines.text: Open AUT's Special Consideration Application (SCA) tool. The link is on AUT's "Special consideration for an assessment" page.

quotes.text: You must apply using the Special Consideration Application tool

lines.text: The first time, Microsoft asks you to approve access. Click 'accept' and carry on.

quotes.text: When you're accessing the tool for the first time, you'll be asked by Microsoft to approve access to the new software.
Make sure you click on ‘accept’ and proceed.

lines.text: On the second screen, choose 'short extension'.

quotes.text: select ‘short extension’ on the second screen

lines.text: Need more than 3 days because of something serious? Then you need a standard extension, with evidence.

quotes.text: If you need more time than 3 days because of valid exceptional circumstances, you need to apply for the standard extension and provide evidence

lines.text: The page doesn't say how you'll hear that your short extension is confirmed, or what your new due time is. If you're unsure, contact the Student Hub: studenthub@aut.ac.nz or 0800 288 864.

quotes.text: Email: studenthub@aut.ac.nz

lines.text: If something serious is affecting you, you can apply for special consideration instead. You'll need to provide evidence.

quotes.text: If this happens, you can apply for special consideration for that assessment.
If you need more time than 3 days because of valid exceptional circumstances, you need to apply for the standard extension and provide evidence
If you need further extensions for the same course, you'll then need to provide evidence of exceptional circumstances.

lines.text: Missed the short-extension deadline? You can still apply for special consideration, up to 5 working days after the due date.

quotes.text: You can submit an SCA up to 5 working days after your assessment due date.

lines.text: The page offers nothing else if you simply need more time. If you're unsure, contact the Student Hub: studenthub@aut.ac.nz or 0800 288 864.

quotes.text: Email: studenthub@aut.ac.nz

lines.text: Special consideration is for when something serious, beyond your control, affects an assessment. Pick the closest match.

quotes.text: seriously affected by exceptional circumstances beyond your control

options.label: Bereavement, being a victim of crime, or something else
A sporting, cultural, religious or AUT commitment
Computer or printer trouble, lost work, or I misread the date

steps.title: You need a Student Impairment Report

lines.text: For a medical reason, send a Student Impairment Report with your application. A suitably qualified person fills it in.

quotes.text: you need to provide a completed Student Impairment Report to accompany your Special Consideration Application form.
The Student Impairment Report must be completed by a suitably qualified person.

lines.text: COVID-19 counts: if you're unwell or isolating, have ongoing effects, or your whānau or household has been seriously affected. Choose the 'Medical' reason.

quotes.text: You can apply for a special consideration for assessment if you have COVID-19 and are unwell or you’re needing to isolate.
You can also apply if you're suffering from ongoing health effects due to COVID-19 or your whānau or household has been seriously affected by COVID-19.
Use the ‘Medical’ reason for application.

lines.text: If you couldn't see anyone in time through no fault of your own, that can be taken into account.

quotes.text: though delays in accessing medical care through no fault of your own can be taken into account

ask.question: Who will fill in your report?

options.label: A nurse at the AUT Student Medical Centre
My own doctor or practitioner outside AUT

lines.text: Ask the registered nurses at the AUT Student Medical Centre to fill in your Student Impairment Report.

quotes.text: registered nurses at the AUT Student Medical Centre can complete the Student Impairment Report for your Special Consideration Application.

steps.title: You need a Student Impairment Report

lines.text: If you need support urgently or on an ongoing basis, AUT's Student Counselling and Mental Health services take appointments.

quotes.text: Student Counselling and Mental Health services are also available for appointments if you have urgent or ongoing needs for counselling and/or mental health support.

lines.text: For an emotional or mental wellbeing reason, send a Student Impairment Report with your application. A suitably qualified person fills it in.

quotes.text: you need to provide a completed Student Impairment Report to accompany your Special Consideration Application form.
The Student Impairment Report must be completed by a suitably qualified person.

ask.question: Who will fill in your report?

options.label: A qualified advisor at the Student Hub

lines.text: A qualified advisor at your closest Student Hub can assess you for the report. To book:

quotes.text: For emotional/mental wellbeing impairments, a qualified advisor at the Student Hub can assess you for a Student Impairment Report.

lines.text: Log in to My AUT.

quotes.text: Visit My AUT and log in

lines.text: Click 'Make a booking'.

quotes.text: Click on 'Make a booking'

lines.text: Choose 'Book a Student Hub appointment'.

quotes.text: Select 'Book a Student Hub appointment'

lines.text: Click the 'Special Consideration Application' button.

quotes.text: Click on the 'Special Consideration Application' button

lines.text: Download the Student Impairment Report so your practitioner can fill it in. The form is linked from AUT's "Special consideration for an assessment" page.

quotes.text: If you're seeing an external practitioner, you should download the Student Impairment Report so they can complete it for submission.

lines.text: Bereavement, being a victim of crime, and other circumstances can all count.

quotes.text: Bereavement
Being a victim of crime
Other circumstances

lines.text: What you need to send depends on your situation. The application form explains it.

quotes.text: The specific requirements for your application will depend on the situation and are explained in the Special Consideration Application (SCA) form.

lines.text: For essential sporting, cultural or religious commitments, and AUT-related commitments, applications must be made before the date of the commitment.

quotes.text: Essential sporting, cultural or religious commitments (applications must be made before the date of the commitment)
AUT-related commitments (applications must be made before the date of the commitment)

lines.text: What you need to send depends on your situation. The application form explains it.

quotes.text: The specific requirements for your application will depend on the situation and are explained in the Special Consideration Application (SCA) form.

ask.question: Has the date of the commitment passed?

lines.text: The page says applications for these commitments must be made before the date of the commitment. It doesn't say whether a late application can be considered.

quotes.text: applications must be made before the date of the commitment

lines.text: Contact the Student Hub as soon as you can: studenthub@aut.ac.nz or 0800 288 864.

quotes.text: Email: studenthub@aut.ac.nz

lines.text: AUTSA advocates can also give you advice and support.

quotes.text: AUT Students' Association (AUTSA) has advocates who are there to provide advice and support while you're studying at AUT.

lines.text: AUT does not count these as exceptional circumstances:

quotes.text: Exceptional circumstances do not include:

lines.text: Misreading assessment dates, times or instructions.

quotes.text: Misreading assessment dates, times or instructions

lines.text: Computer or printer problems, unless AUT officially announced that its own equipment failed.

quotes.text: Computer problems, including printer problems, unless they relate to an officially notified failure of university equipment

lines.text: Losing data. Keep backup copies of everything.

quotes.text: Losing data – ensure that you keep backup copies of everything

lines.text: A short extension needs no reason, so it may still be possible.

quotes.text: If you don't have exceptional circumstances but simply need a couple of extra days to submit your assessment, you can apply for a short extension (3 days).

options.label: Check if I can get a short extension
AUT announced its equipment had failed
Something serious is also affecting me

steps.title: Is it before or after the due date?

lines.text: You can apply up to 5 working days after the due date (or test or exam date). When your evidence is due depends on when you apply.

quotes.text: You can submit an SCA up to 5 working days after your assessment due date.

options.label: Before the due date, or on the day
After the due date: 5 working days or fewer
More than 5 working days after the due date

steps.title: Apply now: your evidence is due soon

lines.text: Open AUT's Special Consideration Application (SCA) tool and apply. The link is on AUT's "Special consideration for an assessment" page.

quotes.text: To apply for special consideration:

lines.text: The first time, Microsoft asks you to approve access. Click 'accept' and carry on.

quotes.text: When you're accessing the tool for the first time, you'll be asked by Microsoft to approve access to the new software.
Make sure you click on ‘accept’ and proceed.

lines.text: Tell your AUT teaching department as soon as you can. If you don't have a valid reason, or don't tell them in time, you will get a failing grade. The page doesn't say how to tell them or exactly by when.

quotes.text: If you don't have a valid reason for missing the due date or have not notified your AUT teaching department within the required time, you will receive a failing grade for your assignment or examination.

lines.text: Your evidence is due within 5 working days of the ORIGINAL due date, not of when you apply. You may have only a few days left.

quotes.text: You must upload your supporting evidence within 5 working days of the original assessment due date.

lines.text: Medical or mental health reason? The page says the Student Impairment Report should accompany your application, and also that evidence has a 5-working-day deadline. It doesn't say whether the report can come later. If you can't get it in time, contact the Student Hub: studenthub@aut.ac.nz or 0800 288 864.

quotes.text: you need to provide a completed Student Impairment Report to accompany your Special Consideration Application form.
Email: studenthub@aut.ac.nz
